alt: Graph of y = x^2 - 4x from x = 0 to x = 4: the shaded region lies below the x-axis, so the integral is negative (-32/3) but the area enclosed is 32/3 square units.
caption: Figure: the region below the axis gives a negative integral; its area is 32/3

alt: The line y = 2x + 3 lies above the curve y = x^2 between their intersection points (-1, 1) and (3, 9); the shaded region between them has area 32/3 square units, found by integrating (2x + 3 - x^2) from -1 to 3.
caption: Figure: the area between a line and a curve is the integral of top minus bottom

alt: Graph of y = x^2 with P(3, 9): the chord to Q(4, 16) has gradient 7, the chord to the point with x = 3.1 has gradient 6.1, and as Q moves towards P the chords approach the tangent at P, whose gradient is 6.
caption: Figure: chord gradients 7, 6.1, ... close in on the tangent gradient 6 at P

alt: Circle with centre (3, -2) and radius 5, equation (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25; the point (7, 1) is at distance 5 from the centre (a 3-4-5 triangle) and (-2, -2) lies on the circle too.
caption: Figure: the circle (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25

alt: Circle (x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 25 with centre C(2, -3) and the tangent 3x + 4y - 19 = 0 touching it at P(5, 1); the tangent is perpendicular to the radius CP, which has gradient 4/3 while the tangent has gradient -3/4.
caption: Figure: the tangent at P is perpendicular to the radius CP

alt: Graph of y = 2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 2(x - 1)^2 - 8: a U-shaped curve with minimum point (1, -8), x-intercepts (-1, 0) and (3, 0), y-intercept (0, -6), symmetrical about the dashed line x = 1.
caption: Figure: y = 2(x − 1)² − 8 with its vertex, intercepts and line of symmetry

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 2x + 4 crossing the x-axis at x = 1 and at the surd roots 1 - sqrt 5 (about -1.24) and 1 + sqrt 5 (about 3.24) from the quadratic factor, and the y-axis at 4.
caption: Figure: the three roots of the cubic: x = 1 and the surd roots 1 ± √5

alt: Graph of y = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3): the cubic rises from the bottom left, crosses the x-axis at -2, 1 and 3 and the y-axis at (0, 6), and ends at the top right; it is positive between -2 and 1 and beyond 3.
caption: Figure: y = (x + 2)(x − 1)(x − 3) crosses the x-axis at −2, 1 and 3

alt: Cumulative frequency graph of the walking times of 75 learners, plotted at upper class boundaries: (0, 0), (10, 8), (15, 23), (20, 45), (30, 63) and (50, 75); half of the 75 learners, 37.5, is reached between 15 and 20 minutes.
caption: Figure: cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries rise to 75, the total number of learners

alt: The line y = 2x - 2 touches the curve y = x^2 - 4x + 7 at exactly one point, (3, 4): equal roots (discriminant 0) means the line is a tangent.
caption: Figure: with c = −2 the line y = 2x + c just touches the curve at (3, 4)

alt: Graph of f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 10 for 0 to 5: it falls from (0, 10) to the minimum (3, 1) and rises to (5, 5), so the range is 1 to 10; the highest value comes from the end point x = 0, not from x = 5.
caption: Figure: for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5 the range of f is 1 ≤ f(x) ≤ 10

alt: Graphs of y = 2^x (through (0, 1), approaching the x-axis on the left) and y = log base 2 of x (through (1, 0), approaching the y-axis downwards); they are reflections of each other in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x are mirror images in y = x

alt: Histogram of walking times of 75 learners with unequal class widths: frequency densities 0.8, 3, 4.4, 1.8 and 0.6 for the classes 0-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-30 and 30-50 minutes; the tallest bar is 15-20 minutes and the data are skewed to longer times.
caption: Figure: bar height is frequency density (frequency ÷ class width), so the wide classes do not look too big

alt: Curves y = x^3 + 4/x + c for c = 5, -1 and -7 are the same shape shifted vertically, all with gradient 3x^2 - 4/x^2; only c = -1 passes through the point (2, 9), which fixes the constant.
caption: Figure: every constant c gives a curve with the same gradient function; the point (2, 9) picks out c = −1

alt: Graphs of f(x) = (x - 1)^2 + 4 for x at least 1 (vertex at (1, 4)) and its inverse f^-1(x) = 1 + square root of (x - 4) (starting at (4, 1)); the two curves are mirror images in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: f and its inverse are reflections in the line y = x

alt: Velocity-time graph of v = 10 - 10e^(-0.2t): the cyclist speeds up from rest and approaches but never reaches 10 m/s; the area under the curve for the first 5 s is the distance, 50/e, about 18.4 m.
caption: Figure: the cyclist's velocity levels off towards 10 m/s; the shaded area is the distance in 5 s

alt: Displacement-time graph of s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t: s = 0 at t = 0, rises to 4 m at t = 1, falls back to 0 at t = 3, then rises to 4 m at t = 4, so the distance travelled is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 m but the displacement is 4 m.
caption: Figure: s rises to 4 m, returns to 0, then rises to 4 m again: distance 12 m, displacement 4 m

alt: Velocity-time graph of v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9: v is zero at t = 1 s and t = 3 s, negative (moving backwards) between them with a minimum of -3 m/s at t = 2, and returns to 9 m/s at t = 0 and t = 4.
caption: Figure: v = 3(t − 1)(t − 3) crosses zero twice, so the particle turns round at t = 1 and t = 3

alt: Number lines for 2x - 1 > 5 (x > 3, open circle) and 3x + 4 <= 25 (x <= 7, filled circle): the overlap is 3 < x <= 7, which contains the integers 4, 5, 6 and 7.
caption: Figure: two conditions on number lines; the solution is where they overlap, 3 < x ≤ 7

alt: Straight-line graph of lg y against lg x through (0.2, 1.1) and (0.8, 2.6): the gradient 1.5 divided by 0.6 is 2.5, which is the power n, and the intercept on the vertical axis is 0.6, which is lg A.
caption: Figure: for y = Axⁿ the line of lg y against lg x has gradient n and intercept lg A

alt: Graph of V = x(24 - 2x)^2 for 0 < x < 12: the volume of the open box rises to a maximum of 1024 cm cubed at x = 4 cm and falls to zero at x = 12.
caption: Figure: the volume of the box against the cut size x has its maximum, 1024 cm³, at x = 4

alt: Graph of S = 2 pi r^2 + 32 pi / r: the total surface area of the tank falls to a minimum of 24 pi, about 75.4 square metres, at r = 2 m and then rises again.
caption: Figure: the surface area of the closed tank against its radius is least when r = 2 m

alt: Graph of y = |2cos x + 1| for 0 to 360 degrees: starts at 3, falls to a cusp at 120 degrees, rises to 1 at 180 degrees (the reflected minimum), falls to a cusp at 240 degrees and rises back to 3 at 360 degrees.
caption: Figure: y = |2cos x + 1| with cusps at 120° and 240°

alt: Graph of y = |x^2 - 6x + 5| with the line y = 3: the curve is above the line for x < 3 - sqrt 7 (about 0.35), for 2 < x < 4 where the reflected arch pokes above, and for x > 3 + sqrt 7 (about 5.65), giving three pieces.
caption: Figure: |x² − 6x + 5| > 3 has three pieces, marked in red on the x-axis

alt: Graphs of y = |2x - 3| and y = x + 1: the line crosses the V at x = 2/3 and x = 4 and lies above it between them, so |2x - 3| < x + 1 holds for 2/3 < x < 4.
caption: Figure: the line is above the V-shaped graph only between the crossing points x = 2/3 and x = 4

alt: Graph of y = |x^2 - 2x - 8|: cusps at (-2, 0) and (4, 0), the reflected arch peaking at (1, 9) and crossing the y-axis at (0, 8). The line y = 5 meets it four times, y = 9 three times, y = 12 twice.
caption: Figure: y = |x² − 2x − 8| and the lines y = 5, 9 and 12

alt: Normal curve for X ~ N(50, 16): the shaded area between x = 46 (z = -1) and x = 53 (z = 0.75) is 0.7734 - 0.1587 = 0.6147, so about 61% of bream are between 46 cm and 53 cm long.
caption: Figure: P(46 < X < 53) is the shaded area between z = −1 and z = 0.75, which is 0.6147

alt: Normal curve for bream lengths X ~ N(50, 16), mean 50 cm and standard deviation 4 cm: the shaded upper tail beyond x = 55 cm (z = 1.25) has area 0.1056, the probability that a bream is longer than 55 cm.
caption: Figure: P(X > 55) is the shaded tail beyond z = 1.25, which is 1 − 0.8944 = 0.1056

alt: Pascal's triangle for n = 0 to 6: row 4 is 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 (the coefficients of (2 + x)^4) and row 6 is 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1 (the first four coefficients used for (1 + 2x)^6); each number is the sum of the two above it.
caption: Figure: row n gives the coefficients of (a + b)ⁿ; rows 4 and 6 are used in Examples 1 and 4

alt: Segment AB from A(1, -2) to B(7, 6) with its perpendicular bisector 3x + 4y - 20 = 0 through the midpoint M(4, 2) at a right angle; the point (0, 5) on the bisector is the same distance, square root of 50, from A and from B.
caption: Figure: the perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint M(4, 2); every point on it, such as (0, 5), is equidistant from A and B

alt: Forces on a 4 kg block at rest on a rough plane inclined at 25 degrees with friction coefficient 0.6: weight 39.2 N, normal reaction about 35.5 N, and friction up the plane of 16.6 N, which is less than the maximum 21.3 N, so the block does not slip.
caption: Figure: friction needed 16.6 N is below its limit μR ≈ 21.3 N, so the block stays at rest

alt: Forces on a 5 kg parcel sliding down a rough plane inclined at 30 degrees with friction coefficient 0.2: weight 49 N, normal reaction about 42.4 N, friction about 8.49 N up the plane, and the weight component 24.5 N down the plane, giving a net 16.0 N and acceleration about 3.20 m/s squared.
caption: Figure: down the plane 24.5 − 8.49 ≈ 16.0 N is the resultant, so a ≈ 3.20 m s⁻²

alt: Forces on a 2 kg particle in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at 30 degrees: weight 19.6 N down, normal reaction about 17.0 N perpendicular to the plane, and a string tension of 9.8 N up the plane, which equals 19.6 sin 30 degrees.
caption: Figure: along the plane T = 19.6 sin 30° = 9.8 N; perpendicular to the plane R = 19.6 cos 30° ≈ 17.0 N

alt: Graph of y = x^2 - x - 12 crossing the x-axis at -3 and 4; the part of the curve below the axis, marked in red on the axis, lies between the roots, so x^2 - x - 12 < 0 for -3 < x < 4.
caption: Figure: the curve is below the x-axis between its roots, so x² − x − 12 < 0 there

alt: Graph of y = x^2 - 8x + 13 with its minimum at (4, -3) and x-intercepts at 4 - sqrt 3, about 2.27, and 4 + sqrt 3, about 5.73, the two solutions found by completing the square: (x - 4)^2 = 3.
caption: Figure: the solutions of x² − 8x + 13 = 0 are where the parabola crosses the x-axis, symmetrical about x = 4

alt: Conical tank with its vertex at the bottom: at depth h = 4 m the water surface has radius r = h/2 = 2 m; with water entering at 2 cubic metres per minute, V = pi h^3 / 12 gives dh/dt = 1/(2 pi), about 0.159 m per minute.
caption: Figure: because r = h/2, the volume depends on h alone: V = πh³/12

alt: Region under y = x^2 + 1 from x = 0 to x = 2 with its reflection below the x-axis: rotating about the x-axis gives a solid whose cross-section at each x is a circle of radius y = x^2 + 1, so V = pi times the integral of y squared.
caption: Figure: each slice is a disc of radius y, so V = π∫ y² dx between x = 0 and x = 2

alt: Region between y = 4 - x^2 and the x-axis from x = -2 to x = 2, with its reflection below: rotated about the x-axis it forms a closed rugby-ball shape of volume 512 pi over 15 cubic units.
caption: Figure: the limits x = −2 and x = 2 come from solving y = 0; rotating the arch about the x-axis gives a rugby-ball solid

alt: Sector OAB of radius 8 cm and angle 1.2 radians: the arc length is 8 times 1.2 = 9.6 cm, the area is half of 8 squared times 1.2 = 38.4 square centimetres, and the perimeter is 8 + 8 + 9.6 = 25.6 cm.
caption: Figure: a sector of radius 8 cm and angle 1.2 radians

alt: Sector OAB with radius 10 cm and angle 1.4 radians: the chord AB is 12.9 cm, the arc is 14 cm, and the shaded minor segment between the chord and the arc has area 20.7 square centimetres (sector area minus triangle area).
caption: Figure: the minor segment lies between the chord AB and the arc AB

alt: Graph of y = square root of x with its tangent at (25, 5), gradient 1/10: close to x = 25 the tangent and curve almost coincide, so sqrt(25.3) is approximately 5 + 0.1 x 0.3 = 5.03.
caption: Figure: near x = 25 the tangent is a good stand-in for the curve, giving √25.3 ≈ 5.03

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1: the curve rises to a maximum at (1, 5), falls to a minimum at (3, 1) and then rises again; it crosses the y-axis at (0, 1).
caption: Figure: y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 1 has a maximum at (1, 5) and a minimum at (3, 1)

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 2x^2 + 1 with its tangent y = 4x - 7 touching the curve at P(2, 1), where the gradient 3x^2 - 4x equals 4.
caption: Figure: the tangent y = 4x − 7 touches the cubic at P(2, 1)

alt: Tree diagram for two beads taken without replacement from 4 red and 6 white: after a red the second-stage probabilities are 3/9 and 6/9, after a white 4/9 and 5/9; the paths give RR 2/15, RW 4/15, WR 4/15 and WW 1/3, so P(same colour) = 2/15 + 1/3 = 7/15.
caption: Figure: multiply along each path; the second-stage probabilities change because one bead has been removed

alt: Tree diagram: supplier A 0.7 then germinates 0.9 gives 0.63, not 0.07; supplier B 0.3 then germinates 0.8 gives 0.24, not 0.06; P(G) = 0.63 + 0.24 = 0.87 and P(A given G) = 0.63/0.87, which is 21/29.
caption: Figure: second-stage branches are conditional probabilities; P(A | G) = 0.63 ÷ (0.63 + 0.24)

alt: Triangle with vertices A(1, 2), B(7, 4) and C(3, 9) drawn on a coordinate grid; the shoelace method gives its area as 19 square units.
caption: Figure: the triangle ABC whose area is found from its coordinates

alt: Graph of y = sin x for 0 to 360 degrees with the line y = -0.4: they meet at x = 203.6 degrees and x = 336.4 degrees, the two solutions of sin x = -0.4 in the interval, both in the third and fourth quadrants where sine is negative.
caption: Figure: the line y = −0.4 meets the sine curve twice in 0° to 360°, at 203.6° and 336.4°

alt: Graph of y = tan 2x for 0 to 360 degrees with the line y = square root of 3: tan 2x has period 90 degrees and meets the line four times, at x = 30, 120, 210 and 300 degrees, with asymptotes at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees.
caption: Figure: tan 2x repeats every 90°, so tan 2x = √3 has four solutions: 30°, 120°, 210°, 300°

alt: Graph of y = e^(2x) sin x passing through the origin where its tangent is the line y = x with gradient 1, matching dy/dx = e^(2x)(2 sin x + cos x) = 1 at x = 0.
caption: Figure: y = e^(2x) sin x leaves the origin with gradient 1, as dy/dx = e^(2x)(2 sin x + cos x) predicts

alt: Graph of y = 3 sin 2x + 1 for 0 to 360 degrees: two complete waves of period 180 degrees about the centre line y = 1, with maxima of 4 at 45 and 225 degrees and minima of -2 at 135 and 315 degrees.
caption: Figure: y = 3 sin 2x + 1 has amplitude 3, period 180° and centre line y = 1

alt: Circles x^2 + y^2 = 25 (centre origin, radius 5) and (x - 6)^2 + y^2 = 13 (centre (6, 0), radius about 3.61) cross at (4, 3) and (4, -3); the common chord is the vertical line x = 4, at right angles to the line of centres.
caption: Figure: the circles meet at (4, 3) and (4, −3); the common chord x = 4 is perpendicular to the line of centres

alt: Circles with centres C1(1, 2), radius 3, and C2(7, 10), radius 7, whose centres are 10 apart, equal to 3 + 7, so they touch externally at T(2.8, 4.4) on the line joining the centres.
caption: Figure: the centres are 10 apart, equal to the sum of the radii, so the circles touch at one point T on the line of centres

alt: Unit circle with the angle theta measured anticlockwise to the point (cos theta, sin theta) and the angle minus theta measured clockwise to (cos theta, minus sin theta): the two points have the same x-coordinate and opposite y-coordinates, so cos(-theta) = cos theta and sin(-theta) = -sin theta. Quadrants are labelled with the functions that are positive.
caption: Figure: the unit circle shows cos(−θ) = cos θ and sin(−θ) = −sin θ

alt: Vector AB from A(2, -1) to B(8, 7): 6 units across and 8 units up, so AB = 6i + 8j, and its length is the square root of 36 + 64, which is 10.
caption: Figure: the vector AB drawn with its components 6i and 8j

alt: Triangle OAB with OA = a and OB = b; N is the midpoint of OA and M the midpoint of AB, and the dashed line NM equals half of b, so NM is parallel to OB and half its length (the midpoint theorem).
caption: Figure: NM = ½b, so the line joining two midpoints is parallel to the third side

alt: Velocity triangles for a canoe paddled at 2.5 m/s in a river with a 1.5 m/s current: heading straight across gives a resultant of about 2.92 m/s and 72 m of drift in 48 s; aiming upstream at 36.9 degrees makes the resultant 2 m/s straight across, taking 60 s.
caption: Figure: paddle velocity plus current velocity equals the resultant; aiming upstream cancels the drift

alt: Velocity-time graph of the kombi: it accelerates at 2 m/s^2 from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s, travels at 20 m/s until 70 s, then decelerates at 2.5 m/s^2 to rest at 78 s; the area under the graph, 1380 m, is the total distance.
caption: Figure: the area under the velocity-time graph is the distance travelled, 1380 m

alt: Three-circle Venn diagram of 60 households: cattle only 12, goats only 9, chickens only 13, cattle and goats only 7, goats and chickens only 4, cattle and chickens only 6, all three 5, none 4.
caption: Figure: eight regions, filled from the centre (5) outwards; the regions add up to 60

alt: Venn diagram of 40 learners: Geography only 16, both subjects 7, History only 11, neither 6; the circle totals 23 and 18 add to 41 because the 7 in the overlap are counted twice.
caption: Figure: fill the overlap first (7), then each circle's remainder (16 and 11), then the outside (6)
